doc.title: Art Farmer — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Ages, John Henry Lewis, and the high school dance band with his brother
summary: Piano at six, band at thirteen; sousaphone beside John Henry Lewis; Addison on baritone horn; they form a high school dance band playing dances and lodges.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: What age did you start music, and what age, at this point, did you hear this band?
I started the piano when I was either six or seven. When I heard the band, I must have been about thirteen.
By this time, you were playing piano, violin, and now sousaphone.

Yeah, gradually, I was able to grab a cornet. That was the first horn available ‘cause the guys were getting drafted. But before I had the cornet, I was playing the sousaphone, and the other sousaphone player was a man named John Henry Lewis, who used to be world’s light heavyweight champion. He was retired, and we were sitting up there and he was playing the tuba too. It was a nice time.
Was your brother, Addison, at this point also involved in music?

Yes, he was involved in music too. He was playing the baritone horn in this marching band. When the guys went to the army, I was able to get away from the bass horn and get a trumpet. Me and my brother and some other guys our age, we organized a dance band in the high school, and that’s when things really got started.
What kind of engagements did you play, school dances?
School dances and normal dances. We played in little bars and lounges and things.
Did you have societies like Elks Club or Masons?
Yeah, we played in Elks, Masons.
